name: OH-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Jordan's $6M cash on hand vs. challenger's $465
High-profile incumbent with no funded challenge
model.rationale: The district's 21-point Republican lean, Jim Jordan's overwhelming financial advantage, and a Democratic challenger who has raised under $13,000 leave no realistic path to an upset, and prediction markets agree at about 95 percent Republican.
model.watch: A major scandal involving Jordan or an extreme national wave could narrow the margin, though the seat would still very likely remain Republican.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
OH-04 is one of the most Republican-leaning House districts in Ohio, with a partisan lean of roughly 21 points toward the GOP. Jim Jordan, a high-profile incumbent, is seeking another term and holds a large financial advantage, with about $6 million on hand. His Democratic challenger, Joshua Kolasinski, has raised under $13,000 and reported only a few hundred dollars in the bank, and an independent candidate is on the ballot without a visible campaign. No public polls have surveyed the race, and no major race raters have published ratings.

Prediction markets put Jordan's chances around 95 percent. With no polling and minimal challenger activity, the forecast rests on the district's strong Republican lean, Jordan's incumbency and fundraising, and the absence of any outside spending against him. The seat is rated safely Republican, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
